record.paper_title: Global results on rational systems in the plane, part 1
record.original_question: For the nonnegative-parameter planar rational system x_{n+1} = (a1 + b1 x_n + g1 y_n)/(A1 + B1 x_n + C1 y_n), y_{n+1} = (a2 + b2 x_n + g2 y_n)/(A2 + B2 x_n + C2 y_n), with nonnegative initial conditions and positive denominators, suppose a special case has a unique equilibrium and every solution is bounded. Determine whether local asymptotic stability of that unique equilibrium implies global asymptotic stability of the equilibrium.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the planar rational system of difference equations
  x_{n+1} = (a_1 + b_1 x_n + g_1 y_n)/(A_1 + B_1 x_n + C_1 y_n),
  y_{n+1} = (a_2 + b_2 x_n + g_2 y_n)/(A_2 + B_2 x_n + C_2 y_n),
for n = 0, 1, 2, …, where all parameters a_i, b_i, g_i, A_i, B_i, C_i (i = 1, 2) are nonnegative real numbers, the initial conditions (x_0, y_0) are nonnegative, and the denominators are assumed to be positive for all n ≥ 0 along every admissible orbit. An equilibrium (x̄, ȳ) of the system is a fixed point of the map defining the recurrence. Local asymptotic stability of (x̄, ȳ) is defined in the usual sense (Lyapunov stable together with local attractivity), while global asymptotic stability means that (x̄, ȳ) is Lyapunov stable and attracts every admissible orbit in the nonnegative quadrant.

Assume that a particular special case of the above system (i.e., a specification of the parameters within the allowed nonnegative range) has the following two properties:
 (i) the system has a unique equilibrium point in the nonnegative quadrant;
 (ii) every admissible solution of the system is bounded.

Question: Under these assumptions, does local asymptotic stability of the unique equilibrium imply its global asymptotic stability?
artifact.status_search_result: This is a well-known open problem of Camouzis and Ladas concerning planar rational systems. It is the subject of ongoing investigation, with partial results for various special parameter cases, but no general resolution has been published. The broader theme (when local asymptotic stability implies global attractivity for rational equations) remains open as a general principle.

status_evidence.title: When does local asymptotic stability imply global attractivity in rational equations?
status_evidence.snippet: Camouzis and Ladas pose open problems and conjectures on whether local asymptotic stability implies global attractivity for rational difference equations.
status_evidence.claim: The general question of when local asymptotic stability implies global attractivity in rational equations is posed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Global Asymptotic Stability of a Rational System (Hu, 2014)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies global asymptotic stability for particular cases of the planar rational system, contributing partial results toward the Camouzis–Ladas open problems.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial results for specific subcases are available; the general open problem remains unresolved.
